content.intro: An NPS survey is a form that asks customers how likely they are to recommend you on a 0 to 10 scale, then why, so a company can measure loyalty as a single Net Promoter Score and see what drives it. This template keeps the score question first and adds just two follow-ups, so it works in an email, in-app or after support.
content.audience: SaaS teams, ecommerce brands, agencies, clinics and service companies that track customer loyalty quarter by quarter.
useCases: A quarterly relationship survey sent to all active customers
A transactional NPS after onboarding or a support ticket closes
Comparing loyalty across plans, regions or customer segments
Benchmarking before and after a big product or pricing change
tips: Use conditional logic to change the follow-up question by score: ask detractors (0–6) what went wrong and promoters (9–10) what they value most.
Connect the Google Sheets plugin and add a formula column to calculate your NPS automatically as responses arrive.
Send the survey through the same channel each time and at the same point in the customer journey so your scores are comparable.

faq.question: What should an NPS survey include?
faq.answer: The standard question 'How likely are you to recommend us to a friend or colleague?' on a 0–10 scale, an open 'Why did you give that score?' follow-up, and optionally one question about the main reason and one about what to improve. Keep it under a minute.

faq.question: How do you calculate a Net Promoter Score?
faq.answer: Group answers into promoters (9–10), passives (7–8) and detractors (0–6). NPS is the percentage of promoters minus the percentage of detractors, giving a score from -100 to +100.

faq.question: What is a good NPS score?
faq.answer: Any score above 0 means you have more promoters than detractors. Many companies treat 30 or more as good and 50 or more as excellent, but benchmarks vary a lot by industry, so compare yourself mainly with your own past scores.

faq.question: How often should you send an NPS survey?
faq.answer: Most teams run a relationship NPS every quarter or every six months and a transactional NPS after key moments like onboarding or support. Avoid surveying the same person more than a few times a year.
